title: Peroxide
textbookText: In the reaction given above, HBr is added in unsymmetrical alkene. In this reaction addition of hydrogen has occurred in the carbon of 2 hydrogen atoms rather than 1 hydrogen atom. It is according to Markovnikov’ rule. A Russian chemist Vladimir Markovnikov studied a large number of addition reactions of unsymmetrical olefins and he observed two types of isomeric products. It states that, the addition of hydrogen halide or other polar reagent occurs in such a way that the positive part of the reagent goes towards the carbon where there is greater number of hydrogen already in unsymmetrical alkenes or alkynes. Peroxide effect or Kharash effect (Anti-Markovnikov’s rule):

Peroxide If you see this example, you will see that reverse type of reaction as you have seen in Markovnikov’s rule. Addition of only HBr but not HI and HCl to an unsymmetrical alkene in presence of organic peroxide (R – O – O – R) takes place just opposite of Markovnikov's rule. It is due to the peroxide effect. It states that, the addition of hydrogen bromide occurs in such a way that the positive part goes towards the carbon where there is lesser number of hydrogen already in unsymmetrical alkenes or alkynes.

Alkene reacts with ozone in the presence of inert conditions in the presence of carbon tetrachloride or in the presence of ethers. First it forms ozonide then by hydrolysis it gives carbonyl compounds i.e. aldehydes and ketones.
